rows.why: Rows like 2d and 1d0h0m0s0ms depend on whether days are an accepted unit, which is item 1's question. Item 1 accepts only h/m/s/ms and rejects `1d`, but the scenario expects 2d to parse as 172800000.
Item 5 asks whether whitespace around the string is allowed. It rejects all whitespace, but the scenario expects "  45m\n" to be trimmed and parse as 2700000.

Most rows (90, 1.5h, -3s, +3s, 1_0s, ３s) are about decimals, signs, bare numbers and non-ASCII digits, which is item 6's question. Its pick (only unsigned ASCII digit runs followed by a unit) rejects all of them. Other rows touch items 1, 4, 5, 7 and 8. Item 8 conflicts on `05s`, since it accepts leading zeros, but item 6 is the closest overall.

No item asks whether a component may exceed the next unit's range (e.g. 90m) when parsing. Item 2 is about order, and item 12 is about how format_duration normalises, not about what the parser accepts.

Item 2 asks whether units must appear in a fixed order. Its pick requires strictly descending order, which rejects 30m1h, 5ms1s and 1s500ms2s, and also rules out repeats like 1h1h. Item 3 covers repeats only, so item 2 is closer.

Item 9 asks what the maximum duration is. Its limit is 9007199254740991 ms and only totals above it are rejected, so the exact maximum is accepted. The scenario's input does use `d`, though, which item 1's pick rejects.
Item 9 rejects totals above 9007199254740991 and rejects over-long digit runs early, which matches both rows raising ValueError.

Item 12 asks how format_duration chooses among equivalent strings and whether it normalises into larger units. Its pick prints 90000 as `90s` and 5400000 as `90m`, but the scenario expects `1m30s`, `1h30m` and `1d`. The 0 row also conflicts with item 11, which returns `0s` instead of `0ms`.

Formatting the maximum as `104249991d8h59m991ms` requires normalising into days. Item 12's shortest-string rule would pick `9007199254740991ms` (18 characters against 20), and days aren't supported anyway.
No item asks whether format_duration output always parses back to the same number.
No item covers format_duration's input validation (negative, above max, bool, float). Item 10 is about parse_duration's non-string input only.
